negative_reviews.author: tazz_da_inferno
negative_reviews.text:
Ordered sushi for dinner and there is no soy sauce nor wasabi. This happened multiple times with this restaurant. We even gave them a call to highlight it and we were told by their staff it’s part of the sushi order anyways.. and essentially we were told that we don’t have to call to ask for wasabi & soy sauce as it’s standard and part of the order. If anyone out there knows about sushi and Japanese cuisine, sushi without wasabi and soy sauce is like steak without seasoning !!

When tried calling the restaurant after receiving the order, they don’t pick up our call. Reported to deliveroo.

Don’t accept the order if you cannot fulfill. Ppl order for delivery via food based apps for convenience. Given this happened multiple times it’s quite unacceptable.

Daily Pipe 8b feed NOT used for counts (its reviews[] caps positives at 12/site and drops comment-less reviews). negative_reviews = rating<=3 with a non-empty comment; `negatives` counts ALL rating<=3 including those with no comment. url null (not in source). issues: Lunch trade is slow because the site is at the end of the boardwalk, so team members in kimonos handed out vouchers near the lifts and the food court.
Michael asked for community building ideas for the Essex area.
A Lakeside booking campaign with a new video was added (Weekly DPM meeting 17/11).
A complaint about raw or partly cooked prawns was raised at Lakeside and Birmingham, and Sophie is investigating (Birmingham Project Meeting 13/11).
B2B: Slerp 50% off first order emails went to Lakeside and Thurrock workplaces on 12/11, and a meeting with the shopping centre marketing team was requested (B2B weekly report 09/11 to 15/11).
Sales were £5,400 below target but up 17% on the week before, with food variance, drinks variance and Google reviews all green (London KPI meeting 17/11).
Google reviews were 26 five star and one 1 star about missing condiments.
Delivery took £3.6K net but the Deliveroo rating was 4 stars, with high inaccurate orders, a 12.7% rider wait time and complaints about missing wasabi and soy sauce and a salty broth.
Saturday labour ran at 15% with four FOH and four BOH, while Monday reached 32% because salaried managers rose from five to six, which Ziang Lin said the management structure and B2C work need.
A morning table order mix up between L6 and L7 was resolved with complimentary food and dessert.

B2C marketing must move away from the escalators because of centre security, towards high footfall spots such as Bombato Bar and the Christmas market; the big screen TV email was sent, while pop up stand permits and costs are pending.
The cinema ticket discount rises from 10% to 20%, and holiday music and reusable Christmas decorations (£200 to £250 budget) are to go in.
The new AGM is training well (South England weekly report).

Regional focus from Ziang Lin: lift spend per head to £25 by offering a maki roll with every main, run hourly toilet checks, enforce the uniform standard (black trousers or black jeans, black shoes and a white kimono for FOH, no hoodies) and share sales projections with BOH two to three times a day (London KPI meeting 17/11).
